title: Romans Bible Quiz - Chapter 3
description: Ten questions on Romans 3: the advantage of the Jew, the words of Scripture about all being under sin, and righteousness through faith.

questions.text: What does the chapter say the Jews were entrusted with, first of all?
questions.explanation: Asked what advantage the Jew has, the text answers, "Much in every way! Because first of all, they were entrusted with the revelations of God."

answers.text: The promise made to Abraham
The service of the temple
The revelations of God
The land of their fathers

questions.text: What does the chapter say about God and every man?
questions.explanation: It says, "Yes, let God be found true, but every man a liar."

answers.text: Let God be found true, but every man a liar
Let God be feared and every man be silent
God is true and every man is wise
God judges and every man accuses

questions.text: What saying does the chapter report as slander against them, adding that those who say so are justly condemned?
questions.explanation: The text mentions the slanderous report, "Let's do evil, that good may come?" and says those who say so are justly condemned.

answers.text: "Let's sin, for the law is ended."
"Let's keep the law and boast."
"Let's judge the world ourselves."
"Let's do evil, that good may come?"

questions.text: What had they previously warned about both Jews and Greeks?
questions.explanation: The text says they previously warned both Jews and Greeks that they are all under sin.

answers.text: That they would be judged by the prophets
That they are all under sin
That the law was given only to the Jews
That faith was counted to Abraham

questions.text: What do the words quoted from Scripture say about the righteous?
questions.explanation: It is written, "There is no one righteous; no, not one."

answers.text: "There is no one righteous; no, not one."
"The righteous are few among many."
"Only the doers of the law are righteous."
"The righteous shall never be moved."

questions.text: What image does the chapter use for their throat in the words it quotes?
questions.explanation: The quoted words say, "Their throat is an open tomb," and that with their tongues they have used deceit.

answers.text: A sharp sword
A dry well
An open tomb
A burning furnace

questions.text: What comes through the law, according to this chapter?
questions.explanation: It says that by the works of the law no flesh will be justified in his sight, for through the law comes the knowledge of sin.

answers.text: The promise of life
The knowledge of sin
The righteousness of God
The hope of the fathers

questions.text: What does the chapter say about all, in the words that follow "there is no distinction"?
questions.explanation: It says that all have sinned, and fall short of the glory of God.

answers.text: All are justified by the works of the law
All have been entrusted with the revelations of God
All will be judged by Moses and the prophets
All have sinned and fall short of the glory of God

questions.text: By what kind of law does the chapter say boasting is excluded?
questions.explanation: It asks by what kind of law boasting is excluded, and answers, "Of works? No, but by a law of faith."

answers.text: By a law of faith
By the law of works
By the law written in the heart
By the law of the prophets

questions.text: What is the answer the chapter gives to the question whether faith nullifies the law?
questions.explanation: It answers, "May it never be! No, we establish the law."

answers.text: "Yes, the law is nullified."
"The law remains only for the Jews."
"May it never be! No, we establish the law."
"We leave the question to God."
